This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
I’ll give you two ways to do it:

| Method | What you run | Why use it |
|--------|--------------|------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Quick, interactive, works if you have the SDK installed. |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Useful for automation scripts, CI/CD pipelines, or when you prefer pure HTTP calls. |

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** and **NVIDIA GPU Driver API** must be enabled.  
> * You need the **Google Cloud SDK** installed (for the CLI) or OAuth 2.0 credentials (for the REST call).  

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI – One‑liner

```bash
# Replace PROJECT_ID and ZONE with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: install GPU drivers
```

### Optional: Install GPU drivers automatically

Create a file called `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA drivers (recommended for GPU usage)
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

Make it executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

When the instance boots, the script will run and install the latest NVIDIA driver.

---

## 2️⃣ REST API – JSON payload

If you’re calling the API directly (e.g., from a custom application), you can use the following HTTP request.  
Replace `{project}` and `{zone}` with your actual project ID and zone.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  }
}
```

### How to obtain `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN`

Use the Google Cloud SDK or OAuth 2.0 flow:

```bash
gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
```

or

```bash
gcloud auth login
gcloud auth application-default login
```

Then copy the token into the `Authorization` header.

---

## 3️⃣ Verify the instance

After creation, you can check that the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=${ZONE} --command "nvidia-smi"
```

You should see something like:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03    Driver Version: 535.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.2     |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap|         Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
|                               |                      |               MIG M. |
|===============================+======================+======================|
|   0  RTX A6000           Off  | 0000:00:1E.0 Off |                  N/A |
|  0%   35C    P8    15W / 300W |   100MiB / 24576MiB |      0%      Default |
+-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
```

---

### TL;DR

* **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu ...`  
* **REST**: POST to `/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` with the JSON above.  

Both methods will give you a fully‑functional Ubuntu 20.04 VM with an RTX A6000 GPU ready for deep learning, rendering, or any GPU‑heavy workload. Happy computing!
